newsitem.title: UK: Maiden sees improved margins, Q1 trading up.
newsitem.headline: Maiden sees improved margins, Q1 trading up.

text.p: Maiden Group Plc, the outdoor advertising company, sees operating margins strengthening further in 1997 and expects to significantly increase its investment level over 1996, Chief Executive Ron Zeghibe said on Wednesday.

"The year has begun with an excellent trading environment and an encouraging mix of long-established and new clients running significant campaigns in the first quarter of the year," Zeghibe said. "Trading and forward bookings for 1997 are stronger than the first quarter of 1996."
Maiden's shares were marked up 7.5 pence at 324p in mid-morning, although no shares had been traded.
Earlier on Wednesday Maiden said 1996 pre-tax profits rose to 7.95 million pounds ($12.9 million) stg from 2.98 million a year earlier on a pro forma basis. Maiden went public in May 1996.
The 1996 results exclude exceptionals, including a 700,000 stg charge related to the consolidation of its London activities into one headquarters.

Operating margins before exceptionals in 1996 rose to 17 percent from 16 percent in 1995. Turnover increased to 55.1 million stg in 1996, including 2.16 million stg in acquisitions, from 36.5 million stg in 1995.
"As we continue to clean up we would expect to get margin enhancement," Zeghibe told Reuters in a phone interview.
Also on Wednesday Maiden announced it had agreed on terms with Railtrack Plc for a new seven-year concession.

"All the commercial issues have been agreed," Zeghibe said. The new agreement removes an existing cap on investment and removes a clause that increased Railtrack's percentage as Maiden's revenues passed certain benchmarks.
"If we did a better job and achieved more, they took more of it," Zeghibe said. "We've agreed to a new level that is flat."

In addition, every three years Railtrack will extend the contract with Maiden for another three years if the company performs well, which provides Maiden with further incentive for long-term investment, Zeghibe said.

Maiden, which increased investment to 4.1 million stg in 1996 from one million stg in 1995, expects to increase investment in 1997. Maiden, which in 1996 spent one million stg to illuminate 800 billboard panels, expects to illuminate a greater number of panels this year.
Zeghibe said it is premature to detail the amount of investment expected for 1997, but said, "I would expect to see significant increase over last year."

Investment plans for 1997 include illumination of panels, the Railtrack concession, and expansion into the six-sheet panel market under a new concession with Safeway. "We have enough cash to do all that," Zeghibe said. "We generated nine million pounds in free cash flow in '96."
-- Leslie Adler, London Advertising Newsdesk +44 171 542 2815 ($ = 0.618 British Pounds)
